reviews.title: Paywall on everybody
reviews.text:
Calling Yubo free to use is a pretty misleading way of describing it. My complaint isn’t that you offer optional upgrades. It’s that you deliberately restrict the ability to discover and connect with people who have already added you.

I shouldn’t have to pay a subscription just to search for someone who added me, browse through people who have already shown interest, and potentially find a mutual like naturally.

You claim these upgrades are optional, but when basic social discovery features are restricted to the point where connecting with people becomes unnecessarily difficult, it feels less like an optional upgrade and more like a paywall designed to pressure users into subscribing.

Honestly, I’d rather deal with advertisements than have potential connections held behind a paywall. An app designed to help people meet each other shouldn’t make meeting people this unnecessarily difficult.

reviews.title: Yubo: Containment Breach Simulator
reviews.text:
I downloaded Yubo looking for normal human beings to make friends with. Unfortunately, I appear to have entered Site-19 during a catastrophic containment failure.

Within minutes, I encountered unsolicited intimate pictures accompanied by unexplained bank details, a sentient-looking vacuum cleaner named Chloe, a person performing a pig dance outside a medieval castle, and enough overconfidence to power the entire British electrical grid.

Somewhere in the middle of this digital apocalypse, I found ONE normal person who likes romance anime. She is currently the only reason I haven’t evacuated the facility.

The app claims to help people make friends. In reality, it feels like a GTA Online lobby collided with an SCP containment wing, a nightclub, and a suspicious financial institution.

Requested improvements:

* Actual friendship.
* Fewer unsolicited pictures.
* Less suspicious financial activity.
* A functioning containment team for Sector 3.

I came here to discuss anime and make friends. Instead, I witnessed things that would make the Foundation’s Ethics Committee resign.

Final verdict: Site security has failed. Sector 3 is compromised. Send the MTF immediately.

Would not recommend to anyone seeking a peaceful social experience. Would recommend to researchers studying anomalous internet behaviour.

~D-Class personnel, currently requesting extraction.

reviews.title: Decent at best, mediocre at worst.
reviews.text:
Generally speaking the app is fine. I was (so far) able to find at least someone to play games with. 

However, the subscriptions REALLY holds it back. I fully understand the need for it because without it, the app cannot exist, but it SEEMS odd that you can’t see reactions from other people. I get needing to pay for other things but seeing reactions should be free by default. Kinda defeats the whole purpose of the app if you can’t see reactions sent to you, and vice versa. If you’re gonna have reactions and such behind a paywall, then wouldn’t it better to have the ability to unlock reactions by watching ads? Similar to something like “Peeps” for instance. I wouldn’t mind doing that. Though it’s just a suggestion that probably isn’t favorable by most. It’s just frustrating that I have to pay for something so basic that’s the whole purpose of the app to begin with. I understand, but I feel you could add ways where people can interact more freely, while also being able to still profit. 

That’s just my own opinion though.

You can message an account that shows as offline, and within seconds multiple “matches” reply with the same generic, copy‑and‑paste style messages, no matter the time of day.

You get plenty of supposed matches, but when they do respond it’s one‑word answers with no context, personality, or any sign there’s a real person behind the profile. The app feels full of fake accounts, and the conversations read like poorly programmed chatbots rather than genuine people.

reviews.title: App has safety concerns
reviews.text:
From what I’ve experienced on this app. Not only there’s claims on this app that there are concerns about the algorithm. There are instances that there are mods on the app that are supposed to enforce rules about minors being on the same lives with legal adults over the age of 18+ .
The app would ban people for explicit content but more instances than not that there’s explicit content with minors on the app that doesn’t seem to get taken down instantly. To where when the issue has been addressed but doesn’t seem that any actual actions has been taken to assess the problem. Which gives the impression that the moderators pick and choose on how to approach the situation only focuses more on favor of numbers of those who subscribe to the app when downloading it. Which begs the question: do they actually care about the users safety? Or is it just for show just for publicity and profit? Are they just telling us what we want to hear? Or are they truly honoring their guidelines? Frankly I’m uncertain that these circumstances would ever change because it seems like nothing has been done to address the hazardous situation. reviews.title: It’s above average and here’s why…
reviews.text: Most social apps nowadays are purely a paywall haven / money making scheme to the extent that’s it’s not worth having it downloaded given you can’t do anything on it without having to pay for a subscription. Yubo I slightly better however since using it last it’s made a turn towards being like the others. I remember Yubo when you could accumulate some credits or coins if you watched ads. This was a great way to limit any limitations on users who were fine with ads. Now it’s just our regular paywall smothered friend app. Can’t see who liked you. Can’t accept their request and can’t even friend them back so apart from swiping, what’s the point? Do better. I gave two stars because it’s not terrible like the major players out there… yet.
